Ordering, ratings, rank numbers and filter behaviour are correct in all six variations and match the supplied sheet exactly, on both desktop and mobile. The only defect is the collapse / "Show More" behaviour, which is missing entirely in V4, V5 and V6 — a CSS-only divergence between the per-variation stylesheets. Results were identical on Chrome Desktop and Mobile Chrome, with no flakiness.

The brief being tested against

  • 6 variations, each putting a different partner in the #1 spot, per the supplied spreadsheet.
  • Apply the test ranking for All Pets, Cats and Dogs.
  • Revert to the hardcoded ranking when Breeds or Enter Zip is selected. The client confirmed they accept a partner's rating changing on breed select, so ratings revert alongside order. (A deliberate change from the original SWF164, where ratings persisted under every filter.)
  • "Show More" must appear after Trupanion in all variations; its position does not change per variation.
Trupanion sits at position 6 in every one of the six variations, so the collapsed state must show exactly 6 cards, ending on Trupanion.

BUG-01 — V4/V5/V6 never collapse and the "Show More" button is invisible SHIP-BLOCKING

Symptom. V4, V5 and V6 load showing all 10 cards instead of 6. The .cre-t-164-toggle element is injected into the DOM with the correct "Show More" label, but it computes to display: none, so a user can never click it. The native toggle is hidden too. The entire Show More / Show Less feature is therefore absent, failing the client's explicit "Show More after Trupanion in all variations" requirement. Reproduced identically on Chrome Desktop and Mobile Chrome, on both the preview links and the live-behaving force URLs.

Root cause — the per-variation CSS files split into two groups

All six JS files are functionally identical: diffing them (after normalising line endings) shows only whitespace and comment differences outside the partnerRatingData array. Every variation correctly tags ranks 7–10 with .cre-t-164-below-trupanion and toggles body.cre-t-164-collapsed. But the JS relies on CSS to do the actual hiding, and the CSS does not match:

RulevB.css (V1) & va3.css (V3)v4.css / v5.css / v6.css
Hide ranks 7–10 while collapsedpresentMISSING
Show our injected togglepositive rule — display: flex !importantreplaced by a negative rule that never turns it on

The rules present in V1/V3 and missing from V4/V5/V6:

body.cre-t-164-default.cre-t-164-collapsed .cre-t-164-below-trupanion { display: none !important; }
body.cre-t-164-default .plan-repeater[data-unique="comparison-table"] > .cre-t-164-toggle { display: flex !important; visibility: visible; }

V4/V5/V6 instead carry only body:not(.cre-t-164-default) … > .cre-t-164-toggle { display: none; }, which hides the toggle in the reverted state but never shows it in the applied state.

Why this shipped: the header comment in v4.css/v5.css/v6.css asserts the stylesheet is "identical across V1-V6" and that "Show More is entirely native's own DOM mount/unmount — we never manage visibility of the 10 slots ourselves. No defensive 'force visible' rule needed." Both statements are false: the JS hides the native toggle and injects its own clone, so with no positive rule nothing is ever shown or hidden. Hashing the five CSS files (after normalising CRLF) gives two distinct values, not one.

Fix

Port the two rules above from vB.css into v4.css, v5.css and v6.css — or better, point all six variations at one genuinely shared stylesheet, since the partnerRatingData array is now the only legitimate per-variation difference. Then re-verify that the collapsed state shows exactly 6 cards ending on Trupanion.

Evidence — correct vs broken, same region of the page

Filter behaviour — verified live

The gating is implemented as shouldRevert() { return !!(params.breed || params.zipCode); } — pet type is deliberately excluded, which is exactly what the new brief asks for. Verified by clicking the real tabs and by loading the ZIP / breed URL parameters:

Filter stateExpectedObserved

Back to All Petstest order retainedtest order retained — no regression from the old buildPASS
Enter Zip (90210)revert to hardcodedcre-t-164-default removed; order back to Lemonade > ASPCA > Fetch > Embrace > Pumpkin > Figo > Trupanion; native ratings; native toggle restoredPASS
Breed selectedrevert to hardcodedsame full revert as ZIPPASS
The previous SWF164 BUG-01 is genuinely fixed. The old build ran a 250 ms interval that unconditionally re-added the collapsed class, so clicking "Show More" within ~3 s of load was silently undone, and the collapse re-fired on every return to All Pets. In this build runCycle() no longer re-adds the class — it is set once in init() and on a genuine filter-context change. Toggling now sticks immediately, and returning to All Pets no longer re-collapses unexpectedly.

BUG-02 — local v2.css is the wrong file entirely housekeeping

local_testing/Local2/variation/v2.css is dated 2026-09-07 (the other five are 2026-09-22) and contains PAY13's modal CSS — body.cre-t-13-control .cre-t-13-modal-main, .cre-t-13-overlay and friends — with no cre-t-164 rules at all. v2.js was updated.

The CSS actually deployed in Convert for V2 is correct (V2 is a full pass live), so this is a local scratch-file problem only. But anyone QA-ing V2 by local injection will get a false failure. This is the third recurrence of the shared-scratch-file trap on this client, after SWF155 and PAY19 — always grep these files before trusting their contents.

Also verified correct (all six variations)

  • Order matches the sheet exactly in every variation, live, on both viewports — V1 Lemonade, V2 Fetch, V3 Embrace, V4 Pumpkin, V5 Figo, V6 Liberty Mutual at #1.
  • Ratings match the sheet exactly, including the position-locked ladder in V2–V6 (9.6 / 8.5 / 8.1 / 7.4 / 6.7 / 6.5 / 5.9 / 4.8 / 4.5 / 4.3).
  • Rank numbers renumber 1–10 correctly in every variation.
  • The "Best Overall" duplicate card syncs to the new #1 in every variation, and its Lemonade-only app-store blurb is correctly hidden when #1 is someone else.
  • The competing cre-t-135 rating widget is hidden (display: none) under cre-t-164-default in all six, so no double rating renders even though cre-t-135 is co-bucketed on the force URLs.
  • No test-related console errors in any variation — 4 unrelated baseline errors appear on every variant including the control.

Open question for the client

V1's rating ladder is not monotonically descending. Fetch sits at rank 2 with 8.4 while Embrace sits at rank 3 with 8.5 — a lower-scored partner ranked above a higher-scored one, visible to users. This is built exactly as the sheet specifies, so it is not a development defect, but it is worth confirming it is intentional. V2–V6 do not have this issue.

Coverage & limitations of this pass

  • Browsers: Chrome Desktop and Mobile Chrome (Pixel 5) only, as requested. Firefox, Safari, Edge and tablet were not run.
  • Breed filter was exercised via the ?breed= URL parameter. The real MUI #breed-select combobox stays Mui-disabled under synthetic input on this site (a known client quirk), so one manual pass on the real widget is still worth doing.
  • getBestOverallCard() / getPartnerCard() use :has() inside querySelector. Fine in Chrome, Safari 15.4+ and Firefox 121+, but worth checking if older-browser support matters.
  • Duplicate-init guard not tested — re-running the variation JS should not double-inject the toggle.
